statement: A real or complex sequence is a function whose domain is an integer index set such as the positive integers; its analytic content concerns the behavior of the indexed values as the index grows.
scope_limits: Uses the generic function concept already owned by C01/C03; this claim specializes it to sequences in analysis.

statement: A sequence (a_n) converges to L exactly when for every epsilon>0 there exists N such that n>=N implies |a_n-L|<epsilon.
scope_limits: Sequence limits only; function continuity is owned by T02.

statement: A convergent sequence has a unique limit.
scope_limits: Real/complex sequences in the standard metric.

statement: Every convergent real or complex sequence is bounded.
scope_limits: The converse is false without additional hypotheses.

statement: Finite algebraic combinations of convergent real or complex sequences have the corresponding algebraic limits whenever every invoked operation is defined, including quotients whose limiting denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Scalar limit laws; does not re-author C02 arithmetic laws.

statement: Every monotone bounded real sequence converges.
scope_limits: Uses completeness/order properties of the real numbers already owned by C02.

statement: A real sequence converges if and only if it is a Cauchy sequence.
scope_limits: Analytic consequence of completeness of R; C02 retains ownership of the real-number system itself.

statement: Every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence.
scope_limits: Bolzano–Weierstrass for real sequences; generic topology remains outside C05 ownership.

statement: A function f is continuous at a point a in its domain exactly when for every epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that domain points x with |x-a|<delta satisfy |f(x)-f(a)|<epsilon.
scope_limits: Real/complex metric setting used for analysis; generic function identity remains C01/C03 ownership.

statement: For real or complex functions on metric subspaces, continuity at a is equivalent to f(x_n)→f(a) for every sequence x_n→a with x_n in the domain.
scope_limits: Uses T01 sequence convergence as a criterion; it does not transfer T01 ownership.

statement: The composition of functions continuous at the relevant points is continuous at the composed point.
scope_limits: Composition as an algebraic operation is inherited from C03; this claim owns its continuity consequence.

statement: Sums and products of continuous scalar-valued functions are continuous, and quotients are continuous wherever the denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Continuity preservation only; scalar arithmetic itself remains C02 ownership.

statement: If a real-valued function is continuous on [a,b], then it assumes every value between f(a) and f(b).
scope_limits: Intermediate Value Theorem on a closed interval.

statement: A real-valued function continuous on a closed bounded interval attains both a maximum and a minimum there.
scope_limits: Extreme Value Theorem in one-dimensional real analysis; generic compactness ownership is not transferred from future C09.

statement: A function is uniformly continuous on a set when one delta can be chosen for each epsilon independently of the particular pair of points in that set.
scope_limits: Analysis-specific uniform continuity definition.

statement: Every continuous function on a closed bounded real interval is uniformly continuous there.
scope_limits: Heine–Cantor in the interval setting; C09 generic topology remains locked.

statement: The derivative f'(a) is the limit of [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h as h→0 when that finite limit exists.
scope_limits: One-variable derivative only; multivariable derivative belongs to T06.

statement: Differentiability of a one-variable function at a point implies continuity at that point.
scope_limits: The converse need not hold.

statement: If f is differentiable at a, then f(a+h)=f(a)+f'(a)h+r(h) with r(h)/h→0 as h→0, so the derivative gives the first-order linear approximation in one variable.
scope_limits: Analytic linear approximation; geometric tangent interpretation is boundary/example only and remains C04 ownership.

statement: Differentiable functions satisfy the linearity, product, and quotient differentiation rules wherever the quotient denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Standard one-variable differentiation rules.

statement: If f is differentiable at a and g is differentiable at f(a), then g∘f is differentiable at a with derivative g'(f(a))f'(a).
scope_limits: One-variable chain rule; T06 owns the multivariable linear-map form.

statement: If f has a local extremum at an interior point c and is differentiable at c, then f'(c)=0.
scope_limits: Necessary condition at an interior differentiable local extremum; not a sufficient condition for extremality.

statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), then some c in (a,b) satisfies f'(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a).
scope_limits: Mean Value Theorem with its standard hypotheses.

statement: Under the standard differentiability hypotheses, Taylor's theorem represents a function by a finite Taylor polynomial plus a remainder whose form or bound records the approximation error.
scope_limits: Finite-order one-variable Taylor theorem; convergence of an infinite Taylor series is a separate question.

statement: A bounded function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable when its tagged Riemann sums approach one common finite limit as the partition mesh tends to zero, equivalently under standard Riemann/Darboux criteria.
scope_limits: Riemann integration only; Lebesgue integration is T07 ownership.

statement: Every real-valued continuous function on a closed bounded interval is Riemann integrable.
scope_limits: One-variable Riemann theorem on compact intervals.

statement: The Riemann integral is linear: the integral of alpha f+beta g equals alpha times the integral of f plus beta times the integral of g for Riemann-integrable f and g.
scope_limits: Finite scalar linearity of the Riemann integral.

statement: For an integrable function and a point c between a and b, the integral over [a,b] equals the sum of the integrals over [a,c] and [c,b].
scope_limits: Interval additivity of the Riemann integral.

statement: If f and g are Riemann integrable on [a,b] and f(x)<=g(x) throughout the interval, then the integral of f is at most the integral of g.
scope_limits: Order preservation of the Riemann integral; ordered scalar primitives remain C02 ownership.

statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and F(x)=∫_a^x f(t)dt, then F is differentiable on (a,b) and F'(x)=f(x).
scope_limits: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, accumulation-to-derivative direction.

statement: If F is an antiderivative of a continuous f on [a,b], then ∫_a^b f(x)dx=F(b)-F(a).
scope_limits: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, evaluation direction.

statement: A differentiable change of variable with the usual continuity and domain hypotheses transforms an integral according to the substitution rule by multiplying with the derivative of the change of variable.
scope_limits: One-variable substitution theorem; exact hypotheses must be checked in use.

statement: An improper integral over an unbounded interval or near a singular endpoint is defined through a limit of proper integrals and converges only when the defining finite limit exists.
scope_limits: Elementary improper Riemann integration; measure-theoretic integration belongs to T07.

statement: For continuously differentiable functions u and v, integration by parts satisfies ∫_a^b u(x)v'(x)dx=[u(x)v(x)]_a^b-∫_a^b u'(x)v(x)dx.
scope_limits: One-variable integration-by-parts identity derived from the product rule and FTC.

statement: An infinite series ∑a_n converges exactly when its sequence of partial sums converges to a finite limit, and the value of the series is that limit.
scope_limits: T05 specializes T01 sequence convergence to partial sums.

statement: The geometric series ∑_{n=0}^∞ r^n converges to 1/(1-r) when |r|<1 and diverges when |r|>=1.
scope_limits: Scalar geometric series.

statement: If ∑a_n converges, then a_n→0; the condition a_n→0 alone is not sufficient for convergence of the series.
scope_limits: Necessary term test together with its non-converse.

statement: Absolute convergence of a scalar series implies convergence of the series.
scope_limits: Real/complex scalar series.

statement: For nonnegative series, domination by a convergent comparison series implies convergence, while domination of a known divergent series by the tested terms gives divergence in the corresponding comparison direction.
scope_limits: Direct comparison principle for nonnegative terms.

statement: When the limit L=lim |a_{n+1}/a_n| exists, the ratio test gives absolute convergence for L<1 and divergence for L>1; L=1 is inconclusive.
scope_limits: Ratio test under existence of the stated limit.

statement: When the limit L=lim |a_n|^(1/n) exists, the root test gives absolute convergence for L<1 and divergence for L>1; L=1 is inconclusive.
scope_limits: Root test under existence of the stated limit.

statement: If a nonincreasing sequence b_n of nonnegative numbers tends to zero, then the alternating series ∑(-1)^n b_n converges.
scope_limits: Alternating-series criterion; absolute convergence is not implied.

statement: Every power series ∑c_n(x-a)^n has a radius R in [0,∞] such that it converges absolutely for |x-a|<R and diverges for |x-a|>R, while boundary points require separate analysis.
scope_limits: Generic power-series convergence; Fourier series and Fourier coefficients belong to T10.

statement: For a function f defined near a point a in R^n, lim_{x→a}f(x)=L means that for every epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that 0<||x-a||<delta implies ||f(x)-L||<epsilon.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional Euclidean norm setting; generic topology remains outside C05 ownership.

statement: A multivariable function is continuous at a exactly when its value agrees with its limit there in the norm-based sense.
scope_limits: Multivariable continuity specialization of T02.

statement: A map f:R^n→R^m is differentiable at a when there is a linear map A such that ||f(a+h)-f(a)-Ah||/||h||→0 as h→0; this A is the total or Fréchet derivative Df(a).
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional total derivative; C03 owns linear-map primitives, T06 owns their differential role.

statement: When a multivariable map is differentiable, the matrix of Df(a) in standard coordinates is its Jacobian, whose entries are the corresponding partial derivatives.
scope_limits: Coordinate representation only; matrix/vector-space primitives remain C03 ownership.

statement: Differentiability of a multivariable map at a point implies continuity there, but existence of all first partial derivatives at that point alone does not imply differentiability.
scope_limits: Contrasts total differentiability with a weaker coordinatewise condition.

statement: If f is differentiable at a and g is differentiable at f(a), then D(g∘f)(a)=Dg(f(a))∘Df(a); in coordinates the Jacobians multiply in the corresponding order.
scope_limits: Multivariable chain rule; C03 retains ownership of composition and matrix multiplication primitives.

statement: If a scalar-valued function is differentiable at a, then its directional derivative in direction v equals Df(a)v, which in Euclidean coordinates equals grad f(a)·v.
scope_limits: Requires differentiability; directional derivatives existing separately do not by themselves imply a total derivative.

statement: If the relevant second mixed partial derivatives are continuous in a neighborhood, then the mixed partial derivatives agree there in the Clairaut-Schwarz sense.
scope_limits: Sufficient regularity condition; equality is not asserted without appropriate hypotheses.

statement: If f:R^n→R^n is continuously differentiable near a and Df(a) is invertible, then f has a continuously differentiable local inverse near a.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional inverse function theorem; global invertibility is not implied.

statement: Under the standard continuously differentiable hypotheses and nonsingularity of the relevant derivative block, an equation F(x,y)=0 locally determines the dependent variables as a differentiable function of the independent variables.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional implicit function theorem; geometric manifold interpretation remains a C04 boundary.

statement: A continuous function on a rectangular box in Euclidean space is Riemann integrable, and its multiple integral can be evaluated by iterated integration in either order under the standard continuous-function hypotheses.
scope_limits: Elementary multiple Riemann integration; measure-theoretic Fubini/Tonelli belongs with T07-level foundations.

statement: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space, a subset is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.
scope_limits: Heine-Borel theorem used as an analysis-specific compactness result; generic topology ownership remains C09.

statement: A sigma-algebra on a set is a collection containing the empty set and closed under complements and countable unions, hence also under countable intersections.
scope_limits: Measure-theory structure inside T07; not probability specialization.

statement: A measure is a nonnegative extended-real set function on a sigma-algebra with value zero on the empty set and countable additivity on pairwise disjoint measurable sets.
scope_limits: General measure definition; probability measures are a future C07 specialization and are not used as support.

statement: Lebesgue measure on R assigns each interval its length and extends this notion consistently to the Lebesgue measurable sets.
scope_limits: Lebesgue measure foundation on R.

statement: A real-valued function on a measurable space is measurable when inverse images of Borel sets are measurable; equivalent generator criteria can be used in standard settings.
scope_limits: Measurability for real-valued functions; no probability semantics is assumed.

statement: For a measurable real or complex function, absolute Lebesgue integrability means that the integral of |f| is finite; then the Lebesgue integral of f is finite and well defined modulo equality almost everywhere.
scope_limits: Lebesgue integral framework; T04 remains owner of elementary Riemann integration.

statement: If a sequence of nonnegative measurable functions increases pointwise to f, then their integrals increase to the integral of f, allowing the value +infinity.
scope_limits: Monotone Convergence Theorem.

statement: For nonnegative measurable functions f_n, the integral of liminf f_n is at most the liminf of the integrals of f_n.
scope_limits: Fatou's lemma.

statement: If measurable f_n converge almost everywhere to f and |f_n| is bounded by one integrable function g almost everywhere, then f is integrable and the integrals of f_n converge to the integral of f.
scope_limits: Dominated Convergence Theorem; the dominating integrable function is essential.

statement: A bounded Riemann-integrable function on a compact interval is Lebesgue integrable there and its Riemann and Lebesgue integrals agree.
scope_limits: Bridge theorem preserving distinct T04 Riemann and T07 Lebesgue ownership.

statement: For 1<=p<infinity, Lp consists of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable functions with finite integral of |f|^p; L-infinity uses essential boundedness.
scope_limits: Measure-theoretic Lp class definition only; T09 owns abstract normed/Banach/operator theory built on such examples.

statement: The complex derivative f'(z_0) is the limit [f(z_0+h)-f(z_0)]/h as complex h tends to zero, and the limit must be independent of the direction of approach.
scope_limits: Complex-variable derivative; C02 owns complex numbers as scalars.

statement: A complex-valued function is holomorphic on an open set when it is complex differentiable at every point of that open set.
scope_limits: Holomorphicity on open subsets of C.

statement: For f=u+iv, complex differentiability implies the Cauchy-Riemann equations; conversely, if the first real partial derivatives are continuous in a neighborhood and satisfy those equations, then f is holomorphic there.
scope_limits: States necessity plus a standard sufficient regularity condition; pointwise equations alone are not asserted sufficient.

statement: Every holomorphic function is analytic: near each point of its domain it is represented by a convergent power series.
scope_limits: Local analytic expansion; T05 owns generic power-series convergence theory.

statement: If f is holomorphic on a simply connected domain, then the integral of f around every piecewise smooth closed contour in that domain is zero.
scope_limits: Cauchy integral theorem in a standard simply connected formulation.

statement: If f is holomorphic on and inside a positively oriented simple closed contour, then each interior value f(z) is given by the Cauchy integral formula involving f(w)/(w-z) along the contour.
scope_limits: Cauchy integral formula under the standard contour/domain hypotheses.

statement: Every bounded entire function is constant.
scope_limits: Liouville's theorem.

statement: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected domain cannot attain a local maximum of its modulus at an interior point.
scope_limits: Maximum modulus principle in its local/interior form.

statement: The zeros of a nonzero holomorphic function on a connected domain are isolated.
scope_limits: Identity-theorem consequence; the identically zero function is the stated exception.

statement: A function holomorphic on an annulus has a Laurent expansion there, and the principal part classifies an isolated singularity as removable, a pole, or essential.
scope_limits: Isolated-singularity classification through Laurent series.

statement: For a meromorphic function with finitely many isolated singularities inside a suitable closed contour and none on it, the contour integral equals 2πi times the sum of the enclosed residues.
scope_limits: Residue theorem with standard contour and singularity hypotheses.

statement: Where a holomorphic function f=u+iv has the required second derivatives, both u and v are harmonic, satisfying the planar Laplace equation.
scope_limits: Complex-analysis relation to harmonic functions; this does not transfer Fourier/frequency harmonic-analysis ownership from T10.

statement: A normed space is a vector space equipped with a norm that induces a metric and hence analytic notions of convergence and continuity.
scope_limits: C03 owns vector-space axioms; T09 owns the added norm-induced analytic structure.

statement: A Banach space is a normed space in which every Cauchy sequence converges to a point of the space.
scope_limits: Completeness in normed spaces.

statement: A linear map between normed spaces is continuous if and only if it is bounded, meaning its output norm is bounded by a fixed constant times the input norm.
scope_limits: Analytic boundedness/continuity of linear maps; C03 retains generic linear-map ownership.

statement: The operator norm of a bounded linear map T is the supremum of ||Tx|| over unit vectors, equivalently the least constant C with ||Tx||<=C||x|| for all x.
scope_limits: Bounded-operator norm.

statement: The continuous dual X* of a normed space X is the vector space of all continuous linear functionals on X, equipped naturally with the operator norm.
scope_limits: Continuous dual in functional analysis; algebraic dual alone is not the object claimed.

statement: A bounded linear functional defined on a linear subspace of a normed space can be extended to the whole space without increasing its norm in the standard Hahn-Banach setting.
scope_limits: Normed-space Hahn-Banach extension formulation.

statement: For a family of bounded linear operators from a Banach space into a normed space, pointwise boundedness implies a uniform bound on their operator norms.
scope_limits: Uniform Boundedness Principle; completeness of the domain is essential.

statement: A bounded surjective linear operator between Banach spaces maps open sets to open sets.
scope_limits: Open Mapping Theorem; Banach hypotheses are part of the claim.

statement: A Hilbert space is an inner-product space that is complete in the norm induced by its inner product.
scope_limits: Hilbert-space analytic structure; C03 owns vector-space primitives.

statement: Every continuous linear functional on a Hilbert space can be represented uniquely as inner product with a fixed vector, with the usual convention-dependent placement of conjugation in the complex case.
scope_limits: Riesz representation theorem for Hilbert-space functionals.

statement: Every vector in a Hilbert space has a unique nearest point in any closed linear subspace, yielding an orthogonal decomposition into the subspace and its orthogonal complement.
scope_limits: Projection theorem for closed linear subspaces; used as a foundation for L2 projection viewpoints in T10.

statement: For an integrable periodic function on the circle, its Fourier coefficients are obtained by integrating the function against the complex exponential frequency modes with the chosen normalization.
scope_limits: Periodic Fourier coefficients; normalization convention must be stated in concrete use.

statement: Distinct trigonometric or complex-exponential frequency modes are orthogonal in the L2 inner product on the circle.
scope_limits: L2 orthogonality of the Fourier system; T09 owns abstract Hilbert-space structure.

statement: The nth Fourier partial sum is the orthogonal projection of an L2 periodic function onto the finite-dimensional span of the frequency modes retained in that partial sum.
scope_limits: Fourier-specific application of T09 projection structure.

statement: For an L2 periodic function, Parseval's identity equates its squared L2 norm with the sum of squared magnitudes of its Fourier coefficients, with constants determined by the normalization convention.
scope_limits: Parseval identity on the circle; explicit constants depend on the chosen convention.

statement: Fourier partial sums of an L2 periodic function converge to the function in L2 norm because the trigonometric system is complete in that Hilbert space.
scope_limits: L2 convergence only; it does not assert pointwise or uniform convergence.

statement: Convergence in L2 norm does not by itself imply pointwise convergence at every point or uniform convergence.
scope_limits: Function-space convergence distinction used to prevent overclaiming Fourier-series behavior.

statement: For f in L1(R), the Fourier transform is defined by integrating f(x) against a complex exponential frequency kernel, with the precise constants fixed by the chosen normalization.
scope_limits: L1 Fourier transform on R; normalization must be declared in concrete calculations.

statement: For suitable L1 functions, the Fourier transform of their convolution equals the product of their Fourier transforms under a consistent normalization.
scope_limits: Convolution theorem in the standard L1 setting.

statement: The Fourier transform of an L1(R) function is continuous and tends to zero at infinity.
scope_limits: Riemann-Lebesgue lemma on R.

statement: After normalization, the Fourier transform extends from a dense L1∩L2 class to a unitary operator on L2(R), preserving the L2 norm in the Plancherel sense.
scope_limits: Plancherel extension on L2; does not assert pointwise integral representation for every L2 equivalence class.
